podcast.title: Explicitly Pro-Communist
podcast.body: The Almanac Singers were a folk group in the 1940s known for being explicitly pro-communist. "Indeed, Guthrie and Seeger had both been members of the Almanac singers, a folk group of the 40s who had been explicitly pro-communist."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 92: "The Lion Sleeps Tonight" by the Tokens

podcast.title: Revolving Door Membership
podcast.body: The Almanac Singers had a constantly changing lineup, with various artists like Burl Ives and Cisco Houston being members at different times. "The Almanac singers had a revolving dorm membership, including everyone from burlives to Cisco Houston at one point or another."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 92: "The Lion Sleeps Tonight" by the Tokens

podcast.title: Shift from Pacifism to War Cheerleaders
podcast.body: The group initially held pacifist views. However, upon the Soviet Union's entry into the Second World War, they immediately reversed their stance and became prominent cheerleaders for the war effort. "They'd been pacifists up until the Soviet entry into the Second World War, at which point they had immediately turned round and become the biggest cheerleaders of the war."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
